newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran police break up three child sex abuse rings.
newsitem.headline: Iran police break up three child sex abuse rings.

text.p: Tehran police have broken up three paedophile rings charged with abusing runaway children in the Iranian capital's poor districts, an Iranian newspaper said on Monday.

The daily Iran said police arrested 10 people, including two notorious criminals known as Davoud Shale (Davoud With a Limp) and Said Eskelet (Said the Skeleton), for sexually abusing the children and then using them for criminal activities.

The "large gangs" were active in Tehran's teeming southern districts where members met their victims near schools or areas frequented by runaways, the newspaper said. It did not say how many belonged to the gangs.
Iranian newspapers rarely report local cases of child sexual abuse which is often cited by the Islamic republic's media as among crimes typical of "morally corrupt" Western societies.
Child rapists can face the death penalty under Iran's Islamic laws.
